general.temas: Recurring stories include the investigation into Gérard Depardieu and Michel Houellebecq on suspicion of gang rape, the police report mentioning Justice André Mendonça and Daniel Vorcaro, the storm in Rio Grande do Sul and the Russian attack on Ukraine. Stories about Black people and racial equality also feature prominently. Only Folha de S.Paulo covers the loss of data center investments.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are concentrated on the Russian attack on Ukraine, which reached Poland and drew condemnation from NATO. In Brazil, prominent stories include the exchange of criticism between São Paulo’s mayor and deputy mayor and judicial news concerning Vorcaro and figures linked to Bolsonaro. The investigation into a suspected gang rape and debates over racial inequality add to social concerns. Stories about culture, science, sports and infrastructure partly balance the overall coverage.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- Kim Jong Un’s daughter appears skiing in images released by North Korean state media.
- São Paulo’s mayor responds with insults to criticism attributed to his deputy; Metro Line 6 will install solar panels.
- Lawyers for Marcola’s brother seek to overturn a robbery conviction and request compensation.
- A Scala executive says Brazil is losing data center investments because it lacks a policy for the sector.
- Coverage includes an investigation into Gérard Depardieu and Michel Houellebecq over an alleged gang rape, as well as news about the Miss Universe pageant and racial equality.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although the insult “an empty head is the devil’s workshop” and the interest in eye-catching aspects of well-known figures stand out.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines São Paulo news and the economy with crime stories and news about well-known figures. No clear political orientation is apparent in the headlines provided.

O Globo.resumen:
- A Russian missile lands in Poland during an attack on Ukraine; NATO condemns “serious violations.”
- A court authorizes Grupo Pão de Açúcar to pay labor debts in 72 installments; Galápagos Capital cuts staff.
- Rio enters Level 3 heat alert, and a foreign tourist dies after an attempted robbery.
- Cleitinho plans to meet Lula to discuss Minas Gerais’ debt; Depardieu and Houellebecq are also under investigation on suspicion of gang rape.
- The front page includes news about health, consumer affairs, entertainment and Brazilian culture.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “massive attack” and “becomes a meme” add intensity or levity, without framing a confrontation between the people and the elites.
O Globo.sesgo: The selection combines international news, the economy and crime stories from Rio with entertainment and consumer news. No clear partisan orientation is apparent in the headlines.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Gadi Eisenkot faces difficulties forming a government in Israel.
- Justice Alexandre de Moraes votes to impose passport and contact restrictions on Flávio Bolsonaro; Janones faces criticism over his response to complaints.
- A storm with winds of up to 114 km/h affects more than 90% of homes in a city in Rio Grande do Sul.
- The ANPD maintains the suspension of Discord live streams in Brazil.
- The front page covers racial barriers in motorsports, artificial intelligence, culture and gastronomy.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “(almost) insurmountable barriers” and “a scene from a movie” add drama.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection pays attention to Brazilian and international politics, alongside social issues, technology and culture. The headline about barriers facing Black talent takes a critical approach to inequality; no definitive political orientation is apparent overall.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- Justice Edson Fachin maintains the pretrial detention of Daniel Vorcaro and a former police officer linked to the case; he also unseals a police report.
- A storm leaves one dead and damages 8,000 homes in Rio Grande do Sul.
- Justice Alexandre de Moraes authorizes the vice president of the Court of Accounts to visit Jair Bolsonaro.
- A survey highlights growth among industrial companies, while Sicredi reports on its rural lending.
- The front page includes news about health, astronomy, history, school textbooks and beach maintenance.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “irritates” and “lashed out” add a degree of emotional charge.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to judicial decisions and economic issues, alongside general-interest news. No clear political bias is apparent in the wording provided.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- Justice Edson Fachin unseals a police report that mentions Justice André Mendonça.
- Countries led by France and Panama call for a clear transition away from fossil fuels at COP31.
- Russia launches more than 110 missiles at Ukraine, according to the front page.
- Several stories address the presence of Black people in politics, music and culture, as well as the work of Afro-Indigenous singer Héloa.
- The front page includes information about payments on the public holiday, soccer, the Libertadores final show, tarot and the horoscope.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although the question “Who is afraid of Black women in politics?” and the assertion that the social structure does not allow them to be anything other than subservient use confrontational language and a generalization.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The selection pays attention to the representation and activism of Black and Afro-Indigenous people. One piece explicitly takes a critical approach to racial and gender inequality in Brazilian politics.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I can see clearly how class struggle works: a court authorized Grupo Pão de Açúcar to pay its labor debts in 72 installments. For the company, it means time; for those waiting for what they are owed, it means an imposed wait. Protecting jobs cannot be used as an excuse to sideline working-class rights.

At the same time, there are calls for an incentive policy to attract data centers. I ask: why offer advantages to big capital without requiring social oversight and collective benefits? Brazil needs public planning, collective ownership of strategic infrastructure and robust public services, not a race to subsidize private investment. The solar panels planned for Metro Line 6 show one possibility: directing technology toward common needs, under democratic control.
opiniones.anarquista:
The authorization for Grupo Pão de Açúcar to pay its labor debts in 72 installments reminds me who is given time when the books don’t balance. For working people, wages are not an abstract figure: they mean sustenance and autonomy. I prefer an economy in which workers decide together about production and its fruits, without depending on the benevolence of bosses or parties.

The storm that damaged thousands of homes in Rio Grande do Sul also raises an urgent question: who decides how to rebuild? I advocate mutual aid networks and neighborhood assemblies capable of organizing resources according to need, without waiting for orders from above. Individual freedom needs that collective solidarity; it does not flourish among people left to fend for themselves or under hierarchies that decide for them.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned that Brazil is losing data center investments, as an executive in the sector warns. The response should not be a race to grant tax privileges to a few companies, but lower taxes, stable rules and fewer obstacles for everyone. An open market allows entrepreneurs and investors to take risks, compete and create opportunities without depending on political favor.

I also see a lesson in the debate over who will pay for future sand replenishment in Itapoá: before committing public resources, the costs, beneficiaries and responsibilities must be clarified. A limited state is not an indifferent state; it is one that protects rights and prudently manages what it collects from citizens. Freedom demands responsibility from both those who govern and those who benefit from their decisions.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
The death of a visitor during an attempted robbery in Rio reminds me that the state’s first duty is to guarantee order. Speeches about inclusion or advertising campaigns are not enough: I want police officers backed by the law, criminals investigated and sentences served. The safety of Brazilians cannot be subordinated to the fashions of the elites.

I am also concerned that Brazil is losing data center investments for lack of a coordinated policy. Sovereignty requires us to control our technological and energy capabilities, not depend indefinitely on decisions made elsewhere. That is why I welcome the Petrobras and Cesar supercomputer with interest. And in the face of proposals to abandon fossil fuels, I support a transition that preserves jobs and national resources. Progress must serve Brazil, not turn the country into an executor of other people’s agendas.
opiniones.centro:
I believe Brazil needs fewer insults and more agreements capable of producing results. The willingness of Minas Gerais’ governor-elect to talk with the federal government about the state’s debt points in that direction: negotiating does not mean giving up on differences, but accepting responsibilities to citizens.

I am also concerned by the warning that the country is losing data center investments for lack of a coordinated policy. Offering tax incentives is not enough: their benefits and costs must be assessed, public finances protected, and the incentives accompanied by clear rules for energy infrastructure. The installation of solar panels for São Paulo Metro Line 6 shows another concrete path: combining investment and innovation with environmental goals.

I support a state that provides certainty to the market, but that is also accountable and protects the public interest.
